newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel in steep contago, jet firm.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel in steep contago, jet firm.

text.p: Singapore gas oil market is in deep contango with a cargo for a prompt date done at a steep discount while a cargo for a forward date in July was done at a higher value, traders said.

"Overall the market is still weak in the short term as stocks remained high but in the outer term it looks more bullish as demand is seen from Indonesia and Vietnam...as well as ahead of the winter period," one trader said.

Traders said a European major sold 150,000 barrels to a Singapore trader at a very steep discount of 65 cents per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, for July 10-14 lifting, on a free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.
"This is one of the lowest (discount) levels I have ever seen, which indicates the steep contango in the market" one trader said.
On the other hand, another 150,000-barrel parcel was sold by a Malaysian trader to the same Singapore trader at $22.00 for a later date range--July 21-25.
This was 10 cents higher than the deal done on Tuesday, indicating buyers' willingness to pay at a higher level for later dates.
Swaps gas oil remained steady, with August traded at $22.85 per barrel.

Traders said gas oil stocks in Singapore remained high, which explained the many offers made especially by refiners and processees. But they noted that regional demand, especially from Indonesia and Vietnam would help to soak up excess supplies.

Despite earlier talk that Indonesia would limit its imports in July to three million barrels, traders now said that the country has already taken about five million barrels for that month, one million barrels over their normal monthly imports.

They said Indonesia has already started making enquiries for August, which were also estimated at around five million barrels. The higher demand was attributed to scheduled shutdowns at the Balikpapan and Cilacap refineries in July and August.
Traders said the closed arbitrage from the Mediterranean would also help limit the growth in supplies and provide some support to prices in the forward months.
A South Korean refiner has resorted to stocking its excess gas oil suipplies in its storage tanks rather than sell at current soft prompt values, traders said.
The shutdowns in Indonesia also prompted the country to take up to three million barrels of jet fuel in July and a projected demand of about the same volume for August.
Indonesia's jet fuel demand was said to be the main reason why jet fuel values have risen over the past two weeks, leading the swaps jet/gas oil regrade to jump to about $2.00 for the prompt month.
Physical values have also risen, trading on Wednesday at $24.20 for July 10-14 between a European major and a US trader.
Traders said the higher jet fuel price would see refiners maximising jet output over gas oil.

Taiwan bought by tender 32,000 tonnes of jet fuel at around $197 per tonne for August 1-10 delivery, c-and-f basis, from a Swiss trader. This translated to about $23.80 per barrel, fob Singapore basis, below current prompt levels.
